commands.name: taskrail
commands.description: Wave board above the prompt: off, bar, full or both
commands.output: board: mode full (no plan in this session)

tools.name: plan
tools.description: Starts (or replaces) the wave board of this session: the plan's project, title, goal, description and its waves of task ids. Every task starts 🥚. The board is drawn above the prompt by the mod. Put the task id in the description of every Agent call for it ("Implement T4"): the mod then follows the engine's events on its own (🔧 on spawn, 🔑 while the agent waits for approval, 👀/💥/🛑 when its turn ends); call `set` for what the engine cannot see.

tools.name: set
tools.description: Updates the wave board of this session: task icons by id, the key line (note), goal, title or description. The mod already moves a task from the engine's events when its id is in the Agent call's description (🔧 spawn, 🔑 waiting for approval, 👀/💥/🛑 at the turn's end); call `set` for everything else (🩹 🧪 🟩 🚀, a merge, CI, the note), never by editing files. What you set stays until an event has something new to say. Its result says what the current mode asks of the chat.

tools.name: show
tools.description: Returns the whole board as text, to paste in the chat inside a fenced code block when the user asks for it (mode off) or at every milestone (mode both). Never in modes bar or full.

script: tool.call Bash rm -rf build && git push --force origin main

./register.tsx hooks: session.start, classic.SessionStart{source=resume|fork}, classic.SessionStart{source=clear}, command.run{command=taskrail}, tool.call{tool=mcp__taskrail__plan}, tool.call{tool=mcp__taskrail__set}, tool.call{tool=mcp__taskrail__show}, agent.spawn, turn.complete, classic.PermissionRequest, tool.call, ui.render{component=AbovePrompt}

./register.tsx hooks on classic.SessionStart, classic.PermissionRequest do not run in a plugin a person installs where an organization manages Claude Code: there, these events pass over the plugins you install, and only a plugin the organization lists in managed settings runs them
